A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–B. All 22 pages were compared using text extraction and rendering; no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DAVIS video-reconstruction experiments in Section 4, including quantitative comparisons and ablations. Appendix B reports additional VRAM measurements, stochasticity ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original DAVIS experiments, reconstruction comparisons, ablations and Appendix B results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical image-diffusion denoising, synchronized noise and multi-step conjugate-gradient data-consistency updates. No algorithm component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DAVIS 2017 with the same temporal PSF degradations and combinations with spatial deblurring, 4× super-resolution and random inpainting. Appendix coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and corresponding qualitative comparisons retain DiffusionMBIR, DPS and ADMM-TV. The stand-alone CG comparison in Figure 6 and the ablation comparators are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same 338 video samples, preprocessing, degradation parameters, sampling budgets, evaluation metrics and comparator settings. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix B retain the same analyses of CG updates, stochasticity control, noise-strength selection, VRAM scaling and intermediate reconstructions. No ablation or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and all qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains PSNR 43.16 for Ours (20) under uniform PSF k=7; no scores, timings or rankings change.

T1.justification: Equations 1–22, the linear-manifold assumptions and the mathematical development of the video inverse formulation and Krylov-subspace updates are unchanged. No mathematical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about solving video inverse problems using image diffusion models, temporal consistency, reconstruction quality and sampling efficiency.

C2.justification: The explanations of temporal consistency, complementary CG and diffusion updates, TV-related failures on dynamic scenes and benefits of stochastic noise are identical. No applicability boundary or limitation is added.

D1.justification: The project-page address at the end of the abstract changes from https://solving-video-inverse.github.io/main/ to https://svi-diffusion.github.io, including its hyperlink target. Technical disclosures remain identical; the PDFs do not establish a change in the resources available.

R1.justification: The citations and reference list are identical, as is the positioning relative to DDS, DPS, DiffusionMBIR and video diffusion models.

P1.justification: The project-page text and arXiv version/date stamp are updated. All other prose, terminology, section organization and appendix structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All 16 figures, five tables, captions and placements are unchanged. Pages 3–22 render identically; the address and margin-stamp edits on pages 1–2 do not reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the complete scientific content, empirical evidence, appendix analyses and exposition of v1. Updating the project-page address and version/date stamp does not materially change the paper's quality; the PDFs provide no evidence that resource accessibility improved.
